chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Mu'alla ibn Muhammad, from Al-Hasan ibn Ali al-Washa, from Asim ibn Humayd, from Malik ibn A'yan al-Juhani, who said:
I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: 'O Malik! Indeed, Allah gives the world to whom He loves and to whom He hates, and He does not give His religion except to whom He loves.'
ai.seo_question: Does Allah give the world to everyone or only to the believers?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi establishes a fundamental theological distinction between general divine grace and exclusive spiritual favor, emphasizing that while worldly prosperity is distributed indiscriminately, true adherence to the religion (al-din) is reserved exclusively for the beloved of Allah. In Shia scholarship, this is often interpreted to mean that the preservation and understanding of divine law are contingent upon divine love, linking spiritual success directly to the criterion of 'hubb' (love). This concept underscores the Shia view that religious authority and piety are not merely legalistic but are deeply rooted in a metaphysical relationship with the Divine.

en.hubeali: Al Husayn Bin Muhammad, from Moalla Bin Muhammad, from Al Hassan Bin Ali Al Washa, from Aasim Bin Humeyd, from Malik Bin Ayn Al Juhny who said,

‘I heard Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> saying: ‘O Malik! Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Gives the world to the one whom He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves and (the ones whom) He<sup>azwj</sup> Hates, and (but) does not Gives His<sup>azwj</sup> Religion except to the one whom He<sup>azwj</sup> Loves’.
en.sarwar: 2. Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad has narrated from Mu’alla ibn Muhammad from al- Hassan ibn Ali al-Washsha’ from ‘Asim ibn Hamidf from Malik ibn ‘Ayun al- Juhni who has said the following: “
I heard abu Ja’far (a.s.) saying, ‘O Malik, Allah grants the world to those whom He loves, and those whom He hates, but He grants His religion only to those whom He loves.’”
